Any website has server logs. Those usually contain the requesting computer's IP address at a minimum. Some sites might keep these forever some for 3 days, but this functionality would have to be explicitly disabled at the web-server level to stop it all together. It would be unheard of for a website with any kind of real traffic numbers not to have server logs. Without digging into the code, I can say that your posting history is mostly definitely stored in Voat's database. It's right there when you click your own username. Comment history, post history, most/least popular comments/posts, and badges. The email you used to create the account is not displayed when going to the user settings page, so maybe they don't store that (but more than likely, the UI is just not showing it and they do keep it in the DB).
If they have server logs, it could be possible to extrapolate which username belongs to an IP, but not without a lot of effort.
